title: What’s Behind the Gerrymandering Arms Race
author: Jacob Eisler
content:
![What’s Behind the Gerrymandering Arms
Race](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/05/Screen-
Shot-2025-08-06-at-10.55.39-PM.png)

The Supreme Court's April 29 decision in _Louisiana v. Callais_ to curb the
scope of Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act has sent shockwaves across
American politics. Loosed from the obligation to [_group
together_](https://www.compactmag.com/article/toward-race-blind-democracy/)
minority voters in dedicated districts, and with partisan gerrymandering now
condoned by the Supreme Court, state legislatures are hurriedly redrawing
districts to benefit their controlling parties. Some states have rapidly
pushed ahead redistrictings to maximize the political power of their parties,
but others have faced obstacles, often posed by their own state constitutions.
The biggest setback so far was faced by Virginia Democrats on May 8, when the
state supreme court
[_voided_](https://www.vacourts.gov/static/opinions/opnscvwp/1260127.pdf?ref=compactmag.com)
a referendum that would have permitted partisan gerrymandering. One
[_particularly
aggressive_](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/10/us/politics/democrats-
virginia-plans-gerrymandering.html?ref=compactmag.com) response proposed by
Democrats would [_drop_](https://www.the-downballot.com/p/how-virginia-
democrats-can-overturn?ref=compactmag.com) the mandatory retirement age of
Virginia Supreme Court justices to 54, thereby purging the bench and allowing
the referendum gerrymander to proceed.

Whatever its excesses in some instances, partisan gerrymandering is a normal
part of American politics. But what is at stake in the current moment of zero-
sum partisanship is a larger shift in the stakes of American democracy. The
focus of leaders is shifting away from maintaining popular support through
effective governance and towards the pursuit of victory through technical
political machination. In other words, the formal game of obtaining power is
increasingly the only one left.
